The best paddling near Koh Samui is in Ang Thong Marine Park, where kayaking is included on all our Ang Thong tours from 1,500 THB (the park is closed 1 November–15 December 2026 and reopens on 16 December). On Samui itself, rent a kayak at Coral Cove for about 300 THB an hour, have a stand-up paddleboard delivered to your beach, or paddle the calm north and north-east bays (Choeng Mon, Maenam, Bophut) on dry-season mornings. Avoid the east coast from October to December, when the north-east monsoon brings swell and red flags.

The east-coast spots are best from February to September and should be avoided in the October–December monsoon; the north and west coasts are calmer for more of the year, but they are tidal and catch offshore wind at times. Pins: Coral Cove · Choeng Mon · Silver Beach · Maenam · Lipa Noi.

Kayaking in Ang Thong Marine Park

Ang Thong is a group of 42 limestone islands north-west of Samui, about an hour away by speedboat, with cliffs, caves and white-sand coves that are made for a kayak. Every one of our Ang Thong tours includes a kayak session, along with snorkelling, the viewpoint and the Emerald Lake. Kayaks are usually sit-on-top doubles, life jackets are provided, and the guide chooses a sheltered stretch of coast for the day's wind. The park fee (300 THB adult, 150 THB child) is paid in cash and isn't included.

Good to know: Ang Thong is closed from 1 November to 15 December 2026 and reopens on 16 December; you can book later dates now. While it is closed, paddle at Koh Tan and Koh Rap from a private longtail or the sheltered south-west coast instead. Compare the Ang Thong boats in speedboat or big boat.

Kayak rental on the beach

Samui doesn't have many dedicated kayak shops. Rentals come from beach vendors, beachfront hotels and the facilities above a few coves.

  • Coral Cove: kayaks for about 300 THB an hour, a cove with rocks to paddle along and some coral to snorkel off the kayak. Wear water shoes: the sand is coarse.
  • Chaweng and Choeng Mon: beach vendors and some resorts rent single and double sit-on-tops by the hour. Agree the price and the time before you go, and check the life jacket fits.
  • Your hotel: many beachfront resorts lend kayaks free or for a small fee to guests, especially in Maenam, Bophut, Choeng Mon and Lipa Noi.

Stand-up paddleboarding: rent, deliver, learn

SUP on Samui works best on flat early mornings on the north and north-east coasts. A rental service based in Maret, See The World SUP Samui, rents and sells boards and delivers them to your hotel or beach, which is the easiest way to paddle where you're staying. Some catamaran charters carry a paddleboard on board, for example the King 9 sailing catamaran (from 7,500 THB per boat for 2.5 hours). If you're new to SUP, start kneeling, stand up with your feet hip-width apart either side of the handle, look at the horizon rather than your feet, and paddle into the wind first so the return is easy.

Paddling around the southern islands

South of Samui, Koh Tan, Koh Madsum (Pig Island) and Koh Rap sit in water that is sheltered from the north-east monsoon, so it is the best paddling area from October to December while Ang Thong is closed. Kayak availability on the islands themselves varies, so the reliable way is a private boat from Thong Krut. Ask for kayaks when you book a private longtail (5,950 THB per boat for up to 8), the three-island private boat (8,450 THB for up to 8) or the Koh Rap full-day private boat (9,950 THB), and we'll tell you what the crew can carry on the day. Koh Rap's long, empty beach and calm bay are ideal for a paddle and a snorkel. Read more in our Pig Island guide.

Mangrove kayaking

A different kind of paddle: our jeep safari with mangrove kayak ends the day with a guided kayak through a mangrove channel, after the Big Buddha, Wat Plai Laem, Hin Ta and Hin Yai and a swim at Na Muang Waterfall. It costs 1,950 THB per adult and 1,650 THB per child from age 5, with lunch, entry fees and transfer included. The water is flat and sheltered, which makes it a good first paddle for children and a rainy-season option when the open sea is rough. See more in our jungle safari guide.

Wind, tide and time of day

Go early. The sea is flattest from sunrise to about 10:00; the breeze usually builds by early afternoon.

Watch for offshore wind. Wind blowing from the land out to sea feels gentle on the beach but pushes a kayak or board away from shore, and it is very hard to paddle back against. On the west coast this happens in the north-east monsoon; on the east coast in a south-west breeze. If the wind is blowing off the beach, stay close in or don't go.

Mind the tide. The north and west coasts have wide, shallow flats at low tide, so you may have to drag a kayak a long way to float it. Launch around mid to high tide. Today's tide: [kp_tide_now]. More in our Koh Samui tides guide.

Safety on the water

  • Wear a life jacket on a kayak, and a leash on a SUP board; the board is your float.
  • Tell someone where you're going and when you'll be back. Take a phone in a waterproof pouch.
  • Stay inside the bay; don't paddle across boat channels, piers or the jet ski area.
  • Sun: a rash vest, hat with a strap and water. Paddling at midday in April burns fast.
  • Jellyfish: box jellyfish are rare but dangerous around Samui. If someone is stung, pour vinegar on the sting for at least 30 seconds, don't rub it, and call 1669.
  • Don't paddle when the beach has a red flag. See beach and swimming safety.

What to bring

  • A rash vest or long-sleeved top, a hat with a strap and sunglasses on a cord.
  • Reef-safe sunscreen, applied 20 minutes before you go out.
  • Water: at least 1 litre per person per hour in the heat.
  • A waterproof pouch for your phone and a little cash.
  • Water shoes for rocky launches such as Coral Cove.
  • Mask and snorkel if you plan to stop at a reef.

Paddling with children

Children can kayak from about 4 or 5 years old in the middle seat of a double with an adult, wearing a fitted child life jacket. Choeng Mon on a calm morning and the mangrove kayak on the jungle safari are the gentlest starts. On our Ang Thong tours, children's life jackets are always provided and must be worn on the boat; put a young child in a double kayak with a parent. Older children who swim well usually love SUP, kneeling first.

Paddling from Choeng Mon to Koh Fan Noi

Koh Fan Noi is the small island just off the north end of Choeng Mon, a short paddle of a few hundred metres across the bay. On a calm morning from January to September it is an easy outing for a confident beginner. At low tide a sandbar joins the beach to the island, so you may walk part of the way; check the tide and come back before it turns. Don't attempt it in the north-east monsoon, when the bay gets choppy, and give way to boats moored off the beach.

Sunrise and sunset paddles

The east and north-east coasts face the sunrise: launch from Choeng Mon or the north end of Chaweng at about 06:00 and you'll have flat water, soft light and the bay to yourself. The north coast at Bophut and Maenam looks across to Koh Phangan, and the west coast at Lipa Noi has the island's sunsets over the Five Islands and the mainland; paddle close to shore, start back before the sun drops, and carry a light if you'll be out after dark. Sunrise is 06:00–06:40 and sunset 17:50–18:40 depending on the month. For more spots, see sunset spots on Koh Samui.

Get on the water

For the best paddling of your trip, book an Ang Thong tour for 16 December onwards, and in the meantime explore the southern islands on the Pig Island small-group longtail (1,750 THB, all year).
